title: The silent-undo check keeps the rewrite excuse when a merge only appends a negation word and every original token survives in order
why: Coordinator 00:38 CST Nov 14 (relayed, from lane ci-wait-cap-55, PR #2839 now fb96825fb59e, lane lint PASS, with runner 10; unchecked by triage): lint/check_silent_undo.py counts an added "never" inside a merge as a reversal (NEGATION; `rewritten` and `extends` in that file: an added negation word voids the rewrite excuse), so a merge that only appends "never past 55 minutes" to main's rule line fails. Each lane that hits it pays a second commit, a force push and a re-check. DONE 09:59 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 09:56, relayed): #3401 merged 09:54:56 CST, main c03312687c13825b46e2cf9f5f2db95c54e84796 (coordinator REST read: merged true 15:54:56Z; ls-remote matches). DIFF READ 09:59 CST Nov 14 (triage, REST file list of #3401; tests not run by triage): extends() in lint/check_silent_undo.py counts negations only up to the last original word in a prose file (.md, .txt, .rst); code, a wordless line and a line with a new comment opener keep the plain rule. The merge-drop test for the appended clause is green by the lane, with code and comment-paste controls.
